COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
D/50 CLCON No.255 of 2024
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
 Mr. Hem Chandra Joshi, Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
 Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Brief Holder for 
respondent no.1.
 Mr. K.P. Upadhyay, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Mr. Hemant Pant, Advocate for 
the respondents.
 It is very strange that the respondents are 
trying to ignore the Court’s order. The Court 
has directed the competent authority to take 
a decision on the question of regularization of 
the petitioner. But, what is being argued on 
behalf of the respondents that the Board of 
Governors have once considered the matter 
and deferred it till the Rules are notified. 
Apparently and admittedly, today there are 
Rules. A decision is to be taken in view of the 
existing Rules. Apparently, the respondents 
failed to take a decision in accordance with 
the existing Rules. Does not it prima facie 
discloses that it is a wilful disobedience of the 
Court’s order? 
 When it is so discussed, the learned State 
Counsel still seeks time to get instruction. 
 List on 13.011.2025. 
 Urgency Application (IA) No.5 of 2025, 
stands disposed of accordingly. 
 
 
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 31.10.2025
Sanjay

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Hem Chandra Joshi, Advocate for 
the petitioner.
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Advocate for 
the respondent no.1.
Mr. K.P. Upadhyay, Senior Advocate, 
assisted by Mr. Hemant Pant, Advocate for 
the respondent nos.2 and 3.
The Court has directed to take a 
decision on a question of regularization of 
the petitioner, but the competent authority 
deferred to the decision, in view of the fact 
that the rules are not notified.
On 31.10.2025, this Court has 
observed that how could it be done? The 
compliance of the order has to be done in 
accordance with the existing rules. Why to 
wait for anything to come in future.
On the last date, when this Court 
noted that “Does not it prima facie 
discloses that it is a willful disobedience of 
the Court’s order?” At that point of time, 
learned State counsel has sought time.
Today, there is no response.
Issue notice to the respondent no.1, 
to personally appear before this Court 
through video conferencing on 12.12.2025.
List 12.12.2025 at 10:30 a.m.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 27.11.2025
Jitendra

CLCON No.255 of 2024
CLCON No.91 of 2025
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Gaurav Kandpal, Advocate 
holding brief of Mr. Hem Chandra Joshi, 
Advocate for the petitioner in CLCON 
No.255 of 2024.
Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate for the 
petitioners in CLCON No.91 of 2025, 
through video conferencing.
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Brief Holder for 
the State/respondent no.1.
Mr. K.P. Upadhyay, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Mr. Hemant Pant, Advocate for 
the respondent nos. 2 and 3.
The Court was informed about the 
disobedience of the Court’s order. In fact, 
the Court had directed to take a decision on 
the question of regularization of the 
petitioners.
The matter was deferred, therefore, 
the respondent no.1 was requested to join 
the proceedings through video 
conferencing.
Today, the respondent no.1 joined the 
proceedings through video conferencing. He 
submits that the operation of the 
regularization rules of 2013 has been 
stayed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court,
which was finally decided sometimes in the 
year 2024. Thereafter, the rules were to be 
modified, which has recently been done on 
05.12.2025. He submits that now, they will 
undertake the process, in view of the 
Court’s directions. He seeks three months’ 
time.  List this matter on 13.03.2026. 
On that date, a statement shall be 
given that the Court’s order has been 
complied with. The Court would not 
consider any further extension, on 
whatsoever ground. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
 12.12.2025
RV
